recipes.name: Honey Roasted Carrots
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Place whole carrots in a baking dish and drizzle with olive oil; toss until carrots are completely covered with oil. Drizzle honey over carrots, then season with salt and pepper; mix until well coated.
Bake in the preheated oven until carrots are just tender, about 30 minutes, or longer if you prefer softer carrots.

raw_recipe.headline: Honey Roasted Carrots
raw_recipe.description: These honey roasted carrots are baked whole, glazed with honey, until deliciously sweet, tender, and caramelized to make a sensational side dish.

video.description: These are truly so simple to make and a perfect easy side dish. These fancy roasted carrots are sweet and savory, with olive oil, honey, salt, and pepper. This side dish doesn’t need much to be a hit!

review.reviewBody: Made using 10 carrots laid out whole on a cookie sheet lined with foil. Needed foil - what a mess - but easy cleanup w/foil. Used no pepper and very little salt. Extremely mild carrot flavor; reminded me of baked sweet potato fries. Still LOOKS like carrots so kids are reluctant to try - however, they can down them without making faces. Will make again! Thanks for the recipe!

I needed to serve more people, so I increased the amount of carrots - doubled. I doubled the honey. Also mixed the honey, olive oil, a bit of red pepper flakes, salt and pepper together before pouring on top of the carrots. Mixed well and them marinate for about an hour. Baked for 50-60 minutes. Used a slotted spoon to remove carrot into serving dish. They were a hit! No leftovers.

Maybe I did something wrong. Followed recipe exactly. Baked for 30 minutes and they were still real firm. Baked another 20 minutes still the same. Finally added water, just enough to cover bottom of the dish. They cooked another 30 minutes before they were tender. Still gave 4 stars because they were really yummy. Any suggestions for next time would be great.

I served these carrots at a Christmas dinner. They were a hit. Good flavor, and so easy to make. Very colorful. I borrowed some ideas from the reviews: my carrots were very fat, so I cut them lengthwise. I partially cooked them in the microwave to slightly soften. Next, I didn't have honey, so I used maple syrup. I blended the maple syrup and oil together, and coated the carrots. I cut the amount of honey (maple syrup) by half, as the original amount seemed excessive. I also used a little less oil then recommended. Lastly, I roasted them in the oven for about 40 min. My results were just as pictured in the recipe! I'll definitely make these carrots again.
Great! 2 lbs of baby carrots per drizzle of Olive Oil, 1/4 cup of Honey and a light sprinkle of Salt and Pepper. Roast for 30-35 minutes uncovered in preheated 350° oven. Stir occasionally. 😋

I used a kilo of carrots cut in half (lengthways) and steamed them for 10 mins to par cook. I left them to cool then used a mix of melted butter, a quality orange honey and salt and pepper then roasted for 50 mins. Decorated with snipped chives and they were lovely. Family guests loved them. I do think the quality of the honey has an impact on the finished result. Don’t just use a cheap squeezy brand or they will just taste sweet. Baking parchment essential!

Great recipe! I use spray olive oil instead of 3 TSP. I spray the pan and spray the carrots. I swish them around and drizzle the honey and salt/pepper. I always cook longer as my family likes them softer! I make them a couple times a month. It’s a nice change from typical veggies!

My family LOVED this!! (Even my toddler who professed not to like carrots asked for seconds). I combined baby carrots, oil, salt/pepper in a plastic bag and shook to coat, then dumped in a foil lined baking dish and eyeball drizzled the honey, making sure to hit each piece. I then popped in the oven and it took close to an hour, but the result is perfection! If my kids will eat it, I will make it - and this is definitely on the make again list! Thanks for such a quick, easy, well-loved veggie dish!!!
It was really easy to make and tasted great. I cooked it longer than the recommended time to soften and amp up the roasted flaver. Will make again!

Delish! Easier and less bake time-
 Just toss carrots (cut in long slices to cut on bake time) with oil and honey in a bowl, and spread into single layer on greased aluminum foil covered baking pan.

I’d give 5 stars but because I add an extra ingredient, I rated 4. I hate baby carrots so I always us whole carrots that I wash and peel. If I have big carrots, I’ll half and sometimes quarter longways just so they will cook evenly. I d everything else according to recipe except I always add either a little minced garlic or garlic powder. It might sound weird but it’s good. Not overpowering, just a hint. Be sure to salt and pepper for the sweet and salty flavor.
Too much pepper and the honey/oil mix burned on the pan.
One dish I must serve at holiday family meals, or be run out of town! Everyone thinks I spend hours on this dish!
Probably worth another shot with more exact measurements. Didn’t really get the honey flavor coming through.
Good. Sweet. Prefer plain roasted carrots.

These roasted carrots were a total win. I was looking for a quick side dish to go with turkey for a friend’s dinner party where everyone was asked to bring a dish, and this recipe was perfect. I didn’t have any honey at home, so I used maple syrup instead—and it worked beautifully. The carrots came out tender, sweet, and full of flavor, with very little effort. All the guests loved the carrots, and they disappeared fast. They’re so good that even a picky kid who usually avoids vegetables might not be able to resist them. Simple, delicious, and a little magical—this recipe is definitely a keeper.

Good basic starter recipe that I would do differently next time. I steamed my carrots first because I like them softer/soggy even. The recipe used too much honey IMO and I would have just did a drizzle afterwards next time. I'll add some extra spices too, like chipotles in adobo sauce or something similar.
love it good really
I made this for a Thanksgiving side and it went over amazingly! I sprinkled minced garlic in the pan and it completed it perfectly.
Delicious and doesn't get any easier, a welcome plus for holiday cooks responsible for multiple dishes.
